newsitem.title: USA: Launch of Mars probe postponed.
newsitem.headline: Launch of Mars probe postponed.

text.p: Bad weather forced NASA on Wednesday to postpone the launch of a probe to explore Mars.

Cloudy skies and rain had threatened the launch and in the end high upper level winds grounded the Delta 2 rocket, which was due to send the Mars Global Surveyor on its 345-million mile voyage to the red planet.
"The launch has been postponed...at about one minute, six seconds prior to launch due to upper level winds," said NASA launch commentator Bruce Buckingham.
Launch was rescheduled for about noon EST (1700 GMT) on Thursday.
The U.S. space agency has just 20 days to get the probe off the launch pad, or faces a wait of 26 months for the planets to realign.
The spacecraft was designed and built in record time to replace NASA's $1 billion Mars Observer probe, which was lost just days before it was due to enter orbit about the red planet.
